title: Requirement status
summary: Label authority and uncertainty instead of treating all statements as requirements.

sections.label: Four statuses
rows: Supported by an approved decision or appropriate source

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: A brief or generated Jira ticket identifies the status of each substantive claim. Unsupported assumptions do not silently become acceptance criteria.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended workflow use: Requirements and evidence, Define the proposed outcome, Recommend go or no-go. Use when drafting a requirement or proposed outcome and when writing a recommendation that must distinguish evidence from suggested next steps. This is an Atlas recommendation reviewed on 2026-10-15, not a mandatory process or an observed execution result.
Check output to obtain: Assign a status and evidence or decision link to every material statement in the brief.
Check output to obtain: Keep observation records distinct from inferred intent and proposed acceptance rules.
Check output to obtain: List unresolved decisions and owners before handoff. An unsupported assumption must not become a confirmed acceptance criterion.

sections.label: Gap review: verified source contribution
sections.text: Reviewed on 2026-10-15: GOV.UK analysis guidance distinguishes observed behavior, interpreted findings and chosen actions. This supports separating evidence from interpretation and decisions. The four Atlas statuses are a local proposed convention, not a status taxonomy defined by the source. Only this added factual contribution was checked in this review. Earlier sections retain their stated proposed or illustrative basis.

catalog.applicability: Use when writing a brief or generating a ticket and each substantive claim needs a label of confirmed, observed, proposed or unresolved, so that unsupported assumptions do not silently become acceptance criteria.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.

claims.text: GOV.UK analysis guidance distinguishes observed behavior, interpreted findings and chosen actions.
